To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inclusion of an emitter SL in a (AlGa) As/ GaAs resonant tun nelling double barrier structure produces a reduction of the threshold voltage, a significant increase of the peak current density, a large enhancement of the LO phonon-assisted current, and novel structure in the magneto-current-voltage characteristics.
the threshold voltage of a resonant tunneller is lowered by the presence of a miniband emitter and that magneto-quantun oscillations are observed in the current-voltage characteristics of the device.

the miniband structure in a SL-based resonant tunneller has been investigated in detail using high magnetic fields, and that the results suggest an increase in LO phonon-assisted tunneling and novel structure in the magnetic field dependence of the current.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a theoretical investigation of resonant tunnellng from miniband emitter (MBE) states in double barrier (DB) structures.
a study of the electrical and magnetic field dependence of the tunnelling properties of a (AlGa) As/GaAs double barrier structure in the presence of a SL in the emitter.
the investigation of the electrical and magnetic field properties of a resonant tunneller with an emitter SL.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the authors have shown that a superlattice in the emitter region of a resonant tunnel diode has a profound effect on both the electrical and the magnetic properties.
the SL emitter states in the double barrier structure are shown to have a significant effect on the electrical characteristics of the device and on magneto-quantised tunnelling.
resonant tunneller devices with a superlattice in the emitter region are more suitable for low voltage and high current operation than conventional resonant tunnellers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the resonant tunnellings of the electrons confined to the emitter SL minibands have been investigated in detail.

the resonant tunnellng structure is a good candidate for the fabrication of a high-speed, low-noise, and high-power device, and that the structure with a superlattice in the emitter is a promising candidate for the fabrication for a high-speed, high-power device.

the inclusion of a SL in an RTDB device results in an increase in the peak current density, an increase in phonon-mediated tunnellng, an increase in the penetration of the wavefunction into the barrier and an increase in the LO-phonon scattering rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a SL as the emitter layer in a double-barrier structure is an effective means of enhancing the tunnelling current and the phonon-assisted tunneling current.
the inclusion of a SL in the emitter of a resonant tunnellng double barrier structure has a profound effect on the tunnelling process.
the SL emitter states in a double barrier resonant tunneller are a rich source of information on electron transport in the emitter barrier and on the tunnelling mechanism.
